title: Saṅkalpa for the upasthāna (morning)

words.gram: f. stem in a compound phrase, written apart
f. stem in a compound phrase, written apart

translation.literal: The morning Sandhyā-Gāyatrī upasthāna I shall perform.
translation.readable: I shall now take leave of the Gāyatrī of the morning Sandhyā (perform her upasthāna).

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga leaves two vowels side by side across a phrase boundary of the formula, without joining them.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, before the upasthāna, the closing worship standing before the deity. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Morning service, step gayatri-upasthana, after the japa; before uttame śikhare.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: S writes the phrase as separate words (प्रातः सन्ध्या गायत्री उपस्थानं); in sense it is one compound, ‘the morning-sandhyā-Gāyatrī-upasthāna’. The vowels of gāyatrī and upasthānam are left unjoined in the witness.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: M has a different wording, प्रातःसन्धोपस्थानं करिष्ये (corrections.json).
